stories.headline: France sees a fourth weekend of cost-of-living protests
body: About 146,000 people protested across France on Saturday, the government said; unions said 250,000.
Police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon.
stories.vc: Persistent protests raise pressure for wage rises and tax changes in France.

stories.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm island as mediators push for calm
body: The US struck Iran's Qeshm island after ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran says it shot down a US MQ-9 drone.
stories.vc: Each new strike near Hormuz adds risk to oil prices and shipping costs.

stories.headline: Houthis say strikes killed 27 in a Sanaa village
body: The Houthis say strikes on a village in Sanaa province killed at least 27 people.
Yemeni government forces say they pushed back Houthi attacks in Marib.
Fighting in al-Jawf entered a third day.
stories.vc: Wider fighting in Yemen keeps Red Sea shipping risks high.

stories.headline: OYO parent PRISM's profit rises 17% ahead of IPO
body: PRISM, OYO's parent, made ₹353 crore profit last quarter, up 17%.
Revenue grew 35% to ₹2,814 crore, though a ₹244 crore tax credit helped profit.
It has filed for a ₹6,650 crore IPO.
stories.vc: OYO's IPO will test investor appetite for big consumer-tech listings.

stories.headline: Karnataka proposes raising the high-rise limit to 24 metres
body: Karnataka proposed defining high-rises as buildings over 24 metres, up from 21.
High-rises face stricter fire and safety rules.
The public has 30 days to object.
stories.vc: Looser rules could cut costs for mid-rise developers in Bengaluru.

stories.headline: Memo says a Chinese exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia's CEO
body: A memo reportedly based on US intelligence says an executive was recruited by China to spy on Jensen Huang.
Nvidia says Huang's dealings with her were not unusual.
It says it does not share classified information with customers.
stories.vc: Spy fears could tighten rules on who can buy Nvidia's advanced chips.
